summary: A satirical article on how Community Learning Centers (CLCs) try to measure their success, set in the fictional borough of Intellectville. It lampoons assessment approaches such as quantified data, anecdotes, standardized tests, charts, attendance counts, efficacy evaluations, dropout feedback, satisfaction surveys and participation, each tied to a colorful character and date. It concludes that the quest for the perfect impact assessment is an endless dance between the measurable and the immeasurable.
one_line: A satirical tour of how Community Learning Centers in Intellectville assess impact, from test scores and attendance to satisfaction indexes and participation.
key_facts: Martina Smartypants, Director of the Learn-a-Lot Hub, asked on September 2, 2023 how to know if a student learned or is just good at filling out Scantrons.

Dr. Numera Tick, a self-proclaimed "Assessment Evangelist," gave a talk on October 10, 2023 called "The 10 Commandments of Quantifiable Enlightenment" arguing that a learner who can't be scored doesn't exist.
Ed U. Cator, facilitator of After-School 'Algebravado,' wrote in a November 18, 2023 newsletter that Maureen's confidence in algebra had soared higher than the Great Eagle Mural.
Sammy Scribbles, advocate for "Anything But Multiple Choice," attempted a pencil boycott on December 4, 2023, which ended abruptly because no one understood the point.
Susan Wizdom, the "High Priestess of Pie Charts," claimed in a January 15, 2024 seminar that a learner's mind could be gauged by the aesthetic beauty of a well-crafted chart.
Benny Beancounter advocates Attendance-Based Success Metrics and spoke at the "Heads in Beds… Er, Seats!" summit on February 8, 2024, holding that a full house means mission accomplished.
Tracy Teachwell and her team of evaluators began an efficacy evaluation on March 20, 2024 with clipboards and questionnaires; the findings were inconclusive but wrapped in jargon.
Larry Laggard, a former CLC attendee and entrepreneur of 'Educational Alternatives,' published the blog post "I Left and Learned" on April 5, 2024, giving dropouts' perspective.
Rita Reportcard unveiled the "Happy Student Index" on May 1, 2024 to capture emotional responses to learning, insisting a happy learner is a successful one.
Fred Facilitatorm promotes 'Participatory Pedagogy' with the mantra "Show Up, Move Up"; his latest workshop was held on June 9, 2024.
The article argues that grants and funding push CLCs toward quantifiable results.
The article is narrated by a reporter who closes by calling the quest for the perfect assessment an educational folie à plusieurs.
